Buyers repeatedly report bookkeeping templates are 'too simple or too complicated' and spend time 'fixing broken formulas'.
Job seekers/contractors discuss estimated-tax and getting-paid friction; Stripe publishes a dedicated freelancer billing guide.

claims.claim: A dedicated US 1099 tax spreadsheet sells real volume at a premium price.
claims.evidence: RunTheCalc '1099 Self-Employed Bookkeeping Spreadsheet': 2.2k sales, 4.7-4.8★ (item avg 4.8/22 reviews), priced ~$17.
claims.interpretation: WTP is proven at ~$17 for a focused, dedicated tool.

claims.claim: Category is deep and premium vs generic bookkeeping.
claims.evidence: '1099 self employed tax tracker quarterly' returns 1,000+ Etsy items; dedicated Schedule-C/quarterly trackers cluster $9-25, well above $1 generic calculators.
claims.interpretation: Niche-specific commands a premium; buyers self-select into the tax framing.

claims.claim: The market is fragmented — no category-owning brand — but breadth shops own Etsy SEO.
claims.evidence: PrioriDigitalStudio (carries a self-employed tax tracker): shop 173.8k sales, 11.1k reviews, 4.8★; but item-level review counts on dedicated trackers stay modest (13-112).
claims.interpretation: No moat, but distribution via Etsy search is dominated by generalist template shops.

claims.claim: Specificity outsells generic — regime/profession versions rank as bestsellers.
claims.evidence: 'Self Assessment UK / HMRC' and 'Therapist Bookkeeping' trackers appear among bestsellers next to generic ones.
claims.interpretation: A US-sub-niche angle (content creator / rideshare / trades) is the wedge.

claims.claim: Recurring complaint: templates are too simple or too complicated and formulas break.
claims.evidence: Bookkeeping-template guidance repeatedly notes buyers 'fixing broken formulas', inconsistent categories, wrong balances at tax time.
claims.interpretation: Correctness + robustness is the differentiator, not features.
